title: The Sump Toad's Rising Pool
story: Deep in the Crystal Mine, Thrennick the Sump Toad squats on the drain and burps floodwater into the tunnels, giggling as it climbs. Three young gem-pickers are stranded on a ledge 27 inches above the water. Mr 6 jams his sword into the clogged drain and the water starts sliding away again — but not fast enough to relax.
question: Thrennick's burps raise the water 7.2 inches every minute, while the unclogged drain lowers it 5.4 inches every minute. How many minutes does Mr 6 have before the water reaches the ledge 27 inches above it?
solution: Water goes up 7.2 inches and down 5.4 inches each minute, so it really rises 7.2 - 5.4 = 1.8 inches per minute.
The ledge is 27 inches up, so the time is 27 / 1.8 = 15.
Mr 6 has 15 minutes before the water touches the ledge.
praise: Working with the rates was exactly right — the missing move was combining the rise and the drain into one net rate before dividing.
hint: Each minute the water gains some and loses some. What is the water's real change in one minute?
victory: Mr 6 hoisted all three gem-pickers out with four minutes to spare, and Thrennick — who had never once done the subtraction — sulked down the drain with a wet, embarrassed plop.
imagePrompt: A bulbous toad monster perched on a mine drain in a flooded crystal tunnel, lantern light glittering off rising water, three children huddled on a high ledge while a brave knightly number six braces a sword in the drain.
